pokemon.verdict: Included in part (judgment (b)). The game has no "magic" category, and physical and special moves fall into the same category of "moves," which is similar to Super Mario RPG. However, in the first generation, whether a move is physical or special is decided mechanically by its type, and special moves have both power and defense decided by the "Special" stat, so the game's own mechanics can tell them apart from physical moves. So the attack moves of the special types (Fire, Water, Grass, Electric, Ice, Psychic, and Dragon), and the support, healing, status ailment, and travel moves with no power, are included as the equivalent of magic. The attack moves of the physical types (Normal, Fighting, Poison, Ground, Flying, Bug, Rock, and Ghost) are not included as physical moves. Moves that look like strikes, such as Honoo no Panchi, Takinobori, and Kurabuhanmā, become special because of their type, so they were included according to the rule.

bravely.overview: The magic in Bravely Default: Flying Fairy is divided into White Magic of the White Mage, Black Magic of the Black Mage, Time Magic of the Time Mage, and Summoning Magic of the Summoner. White, Black, and Time Magic have three spells at each of Levels 1 to 6, and after you buy a spellbook at a shop, the levels you can use are opened up by the job's abilities. The names are shared with FF, and as in Faia -> Faira -> Faiga and Kearu -> Kearura -> Kearuga, the endings "-ra" and "-ga" mark the stage, and "-ga" marks the all-target version, as in Surouga and Heisuga. The differences from FF are that healing became four stages with Kearuda in between, that the wind Earo line went into White Magic and the earth Kueiku line into Time Magic, so that attack magic lines up as five elements (Fire, Water, Lightning, Earth, Wind) times three stages, that the Burizado line is treated as the Water element, and that there are Bēru / Bēruga, which raise evasion. Summoning magic does not use FF summons such as Ifurīto but names from mythology, such as Girutaburiru and Jiusudora no Tsumi, and every one is an attack on all enemies. Because this is the first game in the series, there is no difference from a previous game.
rules: As in FF, changing the ending to "-ra" or "-ga" marks the stage (Faia -> Faira -> Faiga, Earo -> Earora -> Earoga)
Healing has four stages, Kearu -> Kearura -> Kearuda -> Kearuga
Some also use "-ga" for the all-target version (Surou -> Surouga, Heisuto -> Heisuga, Bēru -> Bēruga, Esuna -> Esunaga)
Summoning magic uses proper names from myth and legend instead of the names of summoned beasts (Girutaburiru, Jiusudora no Tsumi, Purometeusu no Hi, Susanoo)
growth: You buy spellbooks at a shop, and the levels you can use are opened by a job's abilities (White Magic Lv 1 to 6 and so on). The Red Mage can use White Magic and Black Magic up to Lv 4
Attack magic and the Kearu line can be made to hit all targets, and the support ability "make anything target all" lets other magic hit all targets too
Summoning magic increases as hermits in various places acknowledge you (Girutaburiru can be used from the start)
Support abilities can change MP cost and power (Black Magic boost, Summoning Magic boost, magic MP saving, and so on)

starocean.overview: In Star Ocean: The Second Story, the technique that corresponds to magic is called "crest arts" (monshōjutsu), and each individual art is called a "spell crest" (jumon). Only the four caster-type characters, Rena, Celine, Leon, and Noel, can use them, and the fighter types use special moves instead. Each user has their own specialty: Rena handles healing and support, Celine handles Fire, Lightning, Star, and Light, Leon handles Water, Darkness, None, and support, and Noel handles Earth, Wind, and healing. There are ten elements: Fire, Water, Lightning, Wind, Earth, Light, Darkness, Star, None, and Negative. Spell crests use MP, and each use raises proficiency and increases power. In the previous game, Star Ocean (the Super Famicom version), the healer Milly's power was called "hōjutsu," separate from crest arts, but in this game the healing spell crests were also brought together under crest arts. In later games in the series, the same technique is called "Sejutsu" (施術) in 3, "Jumon" (呪紋) in 4, and "Juinjutsu" (呪印術) in 5.
rules: Names are English written in katakana that state the effect or appearance as is (Faiaboruto, Aisunīdoru, Ashiddorein, Dīpufurīzu)
"-boruto" is attached to a weak single-target attack aimed at one enemy (Faiaboruto, Sandāboruto, Shadouboruto)
Healing uses "Hīru," "Kyua," and "Fearī" separately, and the healing amount rises in the order Hīru -> Kyuaraito -> Fearīhīru. The all-ally versions are Kyuaōru and Fearīraito
The big moves of the Star and Light elements carry the names of celestial bodies (Sutāraito, Runaraito, Sazankurosu, Meteosōmu, Sutāfurea)
Support spell crests use the English word for the effect as is (Heisuto, Direi, Purotekushon, Sairensu, Gurōsu, Kāsu)
growth: Spell crests are mainly learned by character level. Leon and Noel, who join partway through, already know many spell crests when they join
Celine's Meteosōmu and Leon's Ekusutinkushon are not learned by level but obtained and learned in the hidden dungeon, the Cave of Trials
The more you use the same spell crest, the more proficiency (up to 999) rises, and power, number of uses, and success rate go up

As a mechanic only in the PlayStation version, two spell crests are triggered almost at the same time, and if the elements combine well, "interference" occurs, and the more powerful one absorbs the other and grows stronger

wildarms.overview: In Wild Arms, only Cecilia uses magic (crest magic), and it spends MP. You do not learn magic. Instead, you write two Crests (Jio, Furei, Uingu, Myūzu) in order onto a card-like Crest Graph, and have it made at the Magic Guild in each town. There are 4 x 4 = 16 combinations each for White Magic and Black Magic, for 64 kinds counting lower and upper. The upper versions can be made after you go out onto the open sea, and are often a step above the lower version of the same combination (Bureiku -> Hai Bureiku). Written magic can be erased and rewritten, and you collect everything with 64 Crest Graphs. The names are katakana of English origin, with "Hai" for the upper version, "-Purasu" for the all-target version, and "Mega" above that. There is also top-tier magic that appears only through Randamaizā or Mystic. Summoning is separate from magic and can be used by all three characters as the Force Ability "Materia," which uses the Force Points (FP) that build up during battle and calls the Guardian of an equipped Power Plate. Because it is the first game in the series, there is no previous game. In the later 2nd, the number of Crest Graphs became 32, and in the remake F the distinction between lower and upper disappeared.
rules: Spell names are katakana of English origin (Hīru, Fureimu, Vorutekku, and so on)
The upper version takes "Hai" in front (Hai Hīru, Hai Bureiku)
The all-target version takes "Purasu" at the end (Hīru Purasu, Resutoa Purasu)
The top attacks take "Mega" or have a separate name (Mega Fureimu, Inferuno)
Guardians have proper names (Mua Garuto, Zerutyūkusu, and so on), and the Power Plates, the equipment used to call them, have hiragana names (Rekka no Ikari, Jōsai no Mamori)
growth: Writing two Crests onto one Crest Graph adds one spell. You can also rewrite them
Once you go out onto the open sea, you can make upper magic from the same combinations of Crests
The top-tier magic cannot be made, and occurs by chance or in limited ways through Randamaizā or the equipment Mystic
The power of Materia is decided by the user's magic power (SOR) and is strengthened by Cecilia's Hai Materia

octopath.overview: Octopath Traveler has no independent "magic" command, and the moves that correspond to magic are included in each job's "Battle Abilities." Each of the eight protagonists has a unique base job (Warrior, Merchant, Thief, Apothecary, Hunter, Dancer, Scholar, Cleric) and can attach one more battle job obtained at a shrine. The advanced jobs are Sorcerer, Runelord, Starseer, and Warmaster. Attacks are divided by weapon (sword, spear, dagger, axe, bow, staff) and element (Fire, Ice, Lightning, Wind, Light, Darkness), and "Break," which strikes an enemy's weakness and chips away its shield, is the center of combat. Abilities spend SP, and Boosting with BP raises their power and number of hits. Names are mostly kanji compounds. Some end in "-mahō" (magic), like the Scholar's Kaenmahō and Hyōketsumahō and the Cleric's Kaifukumahō, and others have job-like names such as Onibi, Kazeyobi, Tsukiyo no Uta, and Kujaku no Mai. Because it is the first game in the series, there is no comparison with a previous game.
rules: The magic of the Scholar, Cleric, Sorcerer, and Starseer takes the form "compound word for the effect + mahō" (Kaenmahō, Hyōketsumahō, Kaifukumahō, Fukkatsumahō, Keizokukaifukumahō)
The upper version takes "Dai" or "Tokudai" in front, and the number of hits goes up to 2 or 3 (Kaenmahō -> Daikaenmahō -> Tokudaikaenmahō)
Elemental moves of non-magic jobs have names that suit the job (the Thief's Onibi, the Merchant's Kazeyobi, the Hunter's Raichō, the Apothecary's 氷柱)
Each job has a shared ending: the Dancer uses "-no Mai" (buffs) and "-no Uta" (dark attacks), the Starseer uses "-no Meguri," and the Runelord uses "-no Rūn"
Each job's ultimate move takes the form "title + god's name + no ..." (Sekigakuō Arefan no Chishiki, Seikashin Erufurikku no Michibiki)
growth: You learn a job's abilities one at a time with JP earned in battle. When you have learned the other seven, you learn that job's ultimate move, which can be used only at maximum Boost
Boosting with BP strengthens power, number of hits, healing amount, number of effect turns, and so on

The Scholar's Fire, Ice, and Lightning grow stronger in steps, from all enemies once -> all enemies twice (Dai) -> all enemies three times (Tokudai, advanced job Sorcerer). The Sorcerer also uses Tokudai magic of Wind, Light, and Darkness

xenogears.overview: In Xenogears, what corresponds to magic is called "Ether," and it is used in on-foot combat by spending EP. The name of the special ability differs by character: Fei's is "Kikō," Citan's is "Hijutsu," Rico's is "Kiai," Chuchu's is "Jujutsu," Maria's is "Kisō," and Elly's, Bart's, Billy's, and Emeralda's is "Ether." There are four elements, Wind, Earth, Fire, and Water (there are also non-elemental ones), and Elly's and Emeralda's attack Ethers show their element with a front word, "Rigu" (Wind), "Rudo" (Earth), "Era" (Fire), or "Rei" (Water). The other characters name their moves with kanji technique names (指弾, 小波, 緑掌, and so on), English-style names (Gōrudoshotto, Reddokoron), and each character's own words such as "-no hikari," "-no tate," and "hagane no -." You learn them at set levels as you level up. Many of the same Ethers can also be used while riding a Gear, through the "Ether engine." Because this is the first game in the Xeno series, there is no difference from a previous game.
rules: The name of the special ability differs by character (Kikō, Hijutsu, Kiai, Jujutsu, Kisō, Ether)
Elly's and Emeralda's attack Ethers show the element with the front word (Rigu = Wind, Rudo = Earth, Era = Fire, Rei = Water)
Each character has a consistent way of naming (Billy uses "-no hikari," "Megami no -," and "-no tate," Rico uses "hagane no -," and Bart uses "-koron" and "-mōdo")
Support moves that come in pairs across the four elements put the element name in front to make a set of four (風聖衣 through 水聖衣, 風の盾 through 水の盾, Uindomōdo through Wōtāmōdo)
growth: As a character levels up, they learn Ethers at set levels (only Maria's Gurabiton Hō becomes usable through an event)
Elly learns them in the order single target -> area -> all for each element, and the EP cost also rises 2 -> 6 -> 10
If you use Citan's Renki, his next single-target Hijutsu can be cast on everyone once

valkyrie.overview: Magic in Valkyrie Profile is used only by the Mage job, and there are 23 spells in all, 12 attack spells and 11 healing and support spells. A Mage can learn up to 10 spells, and apart from the starting spells they have when they join, they learn spells by using "spellbooks." There are no points to spend. Instead, using a spell builds up a set amount of CT (Charge Time) for each spell, and you cannot use it again until it returns to 0. The attack spells are two each of six elements, Fire, Ice, Lightning, Holy, Darkness, and Poison, and each one is a standalone spell with no stages. If you set one attack spell at camp, it fires at a single target with a button attack, and if you choose it from the battle commands, some spells target all enemies. A finishing move turns the set spell into its strengthened version (mid-level magic), and if you have a staff that can use grand magic equipped, it becomes a grand magic with a different name for each spell (Fainaru Cheriō and others). Because this is the first game in the series, there is no difference from a previous game.
rules: Many spell names are two English words in katakana joined by a middle dot (Faia Ransu, Dāku Seivā, and so on)
There are two attack spells per element, some whose names include an element word (Faia, Bān, Aishikuru, Raitoningu) and some whose names do not (Kūru Danseru, Igunīto Jaberin, and so on)
Buff spells are paired as "-Reinfōsu" (Gādo / Maito / Superu) and debuff spells as "Redyūsu-" (Gādo / Pawā)
Spells that handle magic are "-Sōsarī" (Rifurekuto / Puribento)
growth: Spells have no stages or upper versions, and strengthening is done with finishing moves. In a finishing move, the same spell becomes a mid-level spell with about three times the number of hits

If you use a finishing move while equipping a staff that can use grand magic, it becomes a grand magic with a set separate name for each spell (Bān Sutōmu -> Ifurīto Kyaresu, Dāku Seivā -> Fainaru Cheriō, and so on)
Learning is by spellbooks. A spellbook can be turned into its paired spellbook by atomic rearrangement

lunar.overview: In Lunar: The Silver Star (the Mega CD version), the magic each party member learns is fixed, and you use it by spending MP. Besides "Magic," the battle menu has "Song" for Luna and "Skill" for Kirī and Temujin. Alex handles fire and healing prayers, Nash handles lightning, Mia handles attack and absorption of fire, ice, earth, wind, spirits, and so on, and Jessica handles healing, ailment cures, and protection. In terms of names, Nash's and Alex's attacks are kanji compounds (Raigeki, Hōraidama, Rekka, Hakunetsuha), Mia's attacks are katakana (Fureimu, Sunōsutōmu), healing is "-no inori" (prayer), support and ailments are "-no juhō" (curse), defense is "-no mamori" (protection), and Luna's songs are "-no uta," so each type has its own pattern. You usually learn them by leveling up, but Alex's first spell "Honoo" is learned at a magic shop, and the dragon magic is learned when you obtain the Dragon Master's equipment. Because this is the first game in the series, there is no previous game. In the remake, Silver Star Story, Alex no longer learns anything but dragon magic, and the party's magic was remade with different names such as Sandāboruto.
rules: Alex's and Nash's attack magic are kanji compounds (Honoo, Rekka, Hakunetsuha / Raigeki, Hōraidama, Raijinga). All of Nash's magic includes the character for "thunder"
Mia's attack magic is English-derived katakana (Fureimu, Aisuatakku, Sunōsutōmu, Kirueā)
Healing is "-no inori" (Sawayaka, Yawaragi, Yasuragi, Ikoi, Iyashi), and support and ailments are "-no juhō" (Minagiri, Izanai, Ayakashi, Mafūji)
Protective magic is "-no mamori," with "en" (circle) for one person and "jin" (formation) for everyone (Hōen no Mamori -> Hōjin no Mamori, Mahōen no Mamori -> Mahōjin no Mamori)

Dragon magic is "[dragon type] ryū no ..." (Rairyū no Kiba, Karyū no Honoo, Suiryū no Sakebi, Chiryū no Ikari). Luna's songs are "-no uta" and use the same words as Jessica's prayers and curses (Sawayaka, Minagiri, Ayakashi, Izanai)
growth: You learn set magic by leveling up. Alex learns "Honoo" at a magic shop, and after that he also learns magic by leveling up
Each time you obtain a piece of the Dragon Master's equipment (Hakuryū no Tsubasa, Sekiryū no Tate, Seiryū no Kabuto, Kokuryū no Yoroi, Arutena no Ken), Alex learns one dragon magic
Several party members may learn the same magic (Yawaragi no Inori by Alex, Jessica, and Mia, and Fureimu by Alex and Mia)

estpolis.overview: Magic in Lufia II: Rise of the Sinistrals (Estpolis Denki II) works by paying money in town shops to buy and learn spells one at a time. Which spells you can learn is fixed for each character, and Guy and Dekar cannot use magic. Maxim can learn fire magic and travel magic, Artea cannot learn instant-death magic, and the Ga Isu line of light attack magic can be used only by Artea. There are four categories: healing, travel, attack, and support. Attack magic has three stages for each of the four elements Fire, Water, Ice, and Lightning, plus two stages of Light and two stages of instant death. The names are distinguished by short katakana separated by a middle dot, such as "Fu Rei," "Uo Mu," and "Re Gi." Magic can target one or several, and when it targets several, the power is divided. Healing magic becomes an attack when used on the undead. In the previous game, Estpolis Denki (Lufia & the Fortress of Doom), magic was learned by leveling up, but in this game it became a purchase system. Many names carry over from the previous game, but the previous game's explosion attack magic of the Ra Gi line, the all-ally healing Esutona and Esutia, and Ansuto, which cures petrification, are gone, and the Ga Isu line of light, Zarujian, which raises magic defense, and Riseto, which resets room mechanisms, were added. The poison cure also changed from the previous game's Poizona to Poizuna in this game.
rules: Attack magic joins "first sound" and "last sound" with a middle dot, and the first sound shows the element (Fire is Fu, Water is Uo, Ice is Ri, Lightning is Re, Light is Ga, instant death is De)
The upper version keeps the first sound and lengthens the back (Fu Rei -> Fu Rea -> Fu Reia, Re Gi -> Re Gio -> Re Gion)
Healing magic begins with "Esu" and lengthens as the stage rises (Esuto -> Esurito -> Esurīto). The ones with revival are Derude and Deruaru
Support magic is short katakana with no middle dot (Difu, Feiku, Mirāru, Surei, and so on)
growth: You buy magic in shops to learn it. You do not learn it by leveling up (the previous game learned it by leveling up)
Attack magic has three stages, beginner, intermediate, and advanced, for the four elements, and two stages for Light and instant death
In the Ancient Cave you start with no magic, and if you obtain it from a red treasure chest, every character who can use it learns it. Mūjiru and Doriddo can be obtained only here

grandia.overview: Magic in Grandia is divided into four elements, Fire, Wind, Water, and Earth, and you cast it by spending MP. When you use a Mana Egg, found in dungeons and the like, at a magic shop, you learn the first spell of one of the four elements (Vān, Hyūi, Keroma, Digan), and that element becomes attached to the character. After that, using magic in battle raises your skill level for each element, and when you reach a set level you learn the next spell. When you have skills in two elements, you also learn magic of the compound elements: Lightning from Fire + Wind, Blizzard from Wind + Water, Forest from Water + Earth, and Explosion from Earth + Fire. Magic has stages of Lv 1 to 3, and you hold MP separately for each Lv. The magic each character can learn is fixed, and Milda and Gido cannot use magic. Feena learns her own Light Wing magic partway through the story, and Liete also has her own magic. Names are mainly short coined katakana words with a shared beginning for each element, as in Vān -> Vanfureimu, Hyūi -> Hyūsurasshu, and Keroma -> Mikeroma. Because this is the first game in the series, there is no comparison with a previous game.
rules: Each element shares a beginning: Fire is "Van" (Vān, Vanfureimu, Vanfurea, Vansutoraiku, Heruvāna) and Wind is "Hyū" (Hyūi, Hyūsurasshu, Hyūnerun)

Healing is based on Keroma, with "Mi" in front for the all-target version, "mu" at the end for the stronger version, and "Makishimu" for the top (Keroma -> Keromamu, Mikeroma -> Mikeromamu -> Mikeromakishimu)
The compound elements also have shared sounds. Lightning is "Rai" (Raiga, Raiden, Tenrai, Ryuurai), Blizzard is "Shaki" (Shakia, Shakīdo), and Explosion is "Zun" (Zunga, Zundeo, Dezun)
Support magic uses short katakana that suggest sound effects, such as Mūnya (sleep), Wao (attack up), Kururu (confusion), and Shin (magic seal)
Character-specific magic has names in kanji or ordinary words, such as Kekkai, Toki no Mon, Seimei no Ki, Owarusekai, Majikaruāto, and Sutāshinfonī
growth: You use a Mana Egg at a magic shop and learn the first spell of one of the four elements (the element you learn is fixed to that character)
Using magic in battle builds up magic experience for each element, and every 100 raises the skill level by 1. When you reach a set skill level, you learn the next spell
When the skill levels of both of two elements reach the conditions, you learn magic of the compound element (Lightning, Blizzard, Forest, Explosion)
Magic is divided into Lv 1 to 3, and the higher the Lv, the higher the power tends to be. You hold MP separately for each Lv
